title: Wavelength-scale optional stopping, critical Feynman-Kac gauges, and capacitary spectral inequalities
summary: We develop two Brownian stopping methods: one uses hitting probabilities and capacity, the other moments of weighted exit distributions. On a closed $m$-dimensional Riemannian manifold, $m\geq 2$, the first gives low-energy spectral inequalities for equilibrium measures supported on sets of zero volume. Combining scales gives heat observability and null controllability from a full-support measure carried by a dense set of Hausdorff dimension $m-2$, minimal under a bounded $H^1$-trace condition.
